item.title: Israel's new $634M German-built 'doomsday' sub gives major boost to Iran deterrence
item.description: The INS Drakon is the largest submarine built in Germany since World War II, carrying a $634 million price tag as Israel bolsters naval power.
item.content:encoded:
Israel has taken delivery of its most advanced and expensive submarine from Germany, expanding its fleet amid escalating regional threats, according to reports.

The handover of the INS Drakon is expected to significantly bolster Israel's underwater strike and reconnaissance capabilities, The Algemeiner reported. The warship had been scheduled to be delivered in 2025.

A statement following the submarine's naming ceremony in Kiel in 2024 said the INS Drakon is of the Dolphin AIP class and "equipped with unique systems, including groundbreaking technologies that expand the range of the IDF's capabilities across various arenas." 

Built specifically for the Israeli Navy by Germany's ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems (TKMS), the submarine is said to provide a vital sea-based layer of "deterrence and retribution," amid the war with Iran, defense analysts say.

Dr. Ehud Eilam, an Israeli national security expert and former researcher for Israel’s Ministry of Defense, told Fox News Digital that maintaining a continuous undersea presence is paramount for the nation's national survival.

TRUMP ADMIN PITCHES 15-POINT IRAN PEACE PROPOSAL AS PAKISTAN OFFERS TO HOLD TALKS

"Some of them would have to be at sea, on high alert, around the clock, if Iran suddenly attacked Israel in such a way that would cripple the IDF, including its strategic capabilities," Eilam said.

"In such a drastic scenario, Israel’s submarine/s that would be at sea could respond," he added.

"Israel’s other submarines might be in Haifa harbor at the time. They might be attacked and unable to operate. This demonstrates how important it is to always have submarines at sea."

TKMS reportedly handed over the INS Drakon—the sixth Dolphin-class vessel and third modified Dolphin II-class submarine in Israel's fleet—at its shipyard in Kiel, Germany, in late July.

US MOVES AIRBORNE TROOPS, MARINES AS IRAN REJECTS CEASEFIRE, RAISING GROUND WAR POTENTIAL

Measuring more than 70 meters (230 feet) in length with a displacement exceeding 2,000 tons, the vessel is reported to be the largest submarine constructed in Germany since World War II, carrying an estimated price tag of $634 million, according to The Algemeiner.

According to Israeli outlet Ynet , Israel's Dolphin-class fleet also provides the nation with a critical sea-based second-strike capability in its defense program.

"Everything is going according to plan with the new program for Israel," TKMS CEO Oliver Burkhard told Ynet Global.

"That also applies to the handover of the last boat of the previous series, including the homecoming in Israel," he said of the expansive submarine program.

The INS Drakon’s arrival comes as Israel projects increasing military power across distant operational theaters, Eilam said.

TRUMP IS PROVING THAT THE WAY TO BETTER OUR MILITARY IS TO SECURE OUR SUPPLY CHAINS

"Israel has been acquiring submarines for several purposes. One of them is for deterrence and retribution, such as if Iran manages to develop nuclear weapons," Eilam said before adding that "Israel has to be ready."

While submarines on active deployment carry out intelligence and reconnaissance missions across the Mediterranean Sea, their primary objective remains readiness for "doomsday scenarios," Eilam noted.

"Israel’s new submarine is bigger than others, which suggests Israel wants to have more options, such as increasing the range of the submarine's missiles so they can reach every target in Iran, even if the Israeli submarine is in the Mediterranean Sea," Eilam said.

"That way the submarine does not have to get closer to Iran, which requires crossing the Suez Canal, and this could be very risky, if not impossible in some situations," he added. "The other alternative is to bypass all of Africa, which would take a long time."

The new submarine was named INS Drakon (Dragon) — a mythical sea creature symbolizing strength, uniqueness and power — was chosen because it contains the Hebrew letters ד׳, ק׳, ר׳ (Dakar), thus commemorating the legacy of the submarine INS Dakar and its crew, the Ministry of Defense said.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Israeli Navy, the Ministry of Defense, TKMS and the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) for comment.

item.title: Tarik Skubal says he was emotional leaving Detroit Tigers for LA Dodgers, would love to return: 'I'm crying'
item.description: Tarik Skubal admitted to crying while saying goodbye to Tigers teammates and called Detroit's offseason acquisitions a World Series-caliber team.
item.content:encoded:
Through no fault of his own, Tarik Skubal has become the center of discussion around Major League Baseball.

Skubal spent his entire career with the Detroit Tigers and, over the last four seasons, has turned himself into one of the best pitchers in baseball. Thanks to the Collective Bargaining Agreement and its handling of a player's first six seasons, he's been paid well below market salaries for a pitcher of his caliber. But Skubal's ready to reach free agency after this season, providing his first opportunity to finally cash in on his hard work and success.

Despite the Tigers' playoff appearance in 2025 and their willingness to spend to try and reach the postseason in 2026, a series of bad breaks, injuries, underperformance, and poor bullpen performance put them well under .500 heading into July. Given the higher prices teams are willing to pay for talent midseason, and the middling return organizations receive if a player leaves in free agency, the Tigers faced a choice. Keep Skubal, hope their season turns around, and potentially watch him leave for just a draft pick this winter, or trade him to a contender for top prospects, years of control, and the certainty that you haven't let your star leave for nothing.

DODGERS REPORTEDLY ACQUIRE ACE TARIK SKUBAL FROM TIGERS IN TRADE THAT STIRS UP MLB WORLD

They traded him. Makes sense, right? Sure, if they'd picked a different team.

But because Detroit chose the offer from the Los Angeles Dodgers, Skubal has unwittingly become a villain around the league. Even worse, he echoed the position shared by players across baseball, like Bryce Harper and Manny Machado, that the Dodgers are not bad for the sport because their owners are willing to accept lower profits in exchange for winning more games.

Many have assumed that the trade means Skubal will spend the rest of his career in Los Angeles. A complete misunderstanding of how midseason trades for free agent rentals work, and an inaccurate assumption that the Dodgers automatically keep every player they trade for.

Well, maybe they'll be happier hearing what Skubal had to say about his upcoming free agency and leaving the only team he's ever known.

TARIK SKUBAL'S DODGERS DEBUT ENDS IN DECISIVE 5-1 LOSS TO CUBS AS L.A. DROPS FIFTH STRAIGHT GAME

"I would love to play my whole career in Detroit. I would love to," Skubal explained in an interview with Pardon My Take. "And hopefully those negotiations can pick back up in November once the playoffs are done. We’ll see where that goes. Hopefully they’re involved with everything. I would love to return."

Skubal also said that his departure was emotional, even as someone who doesn't get emotional easily.

"You start saying goodbye to teammates…a lot of those guys are my best friends," he added. "It’s a bunch of men, and I’m crying. I hate crying. I don’t cry a lot."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

He too felt that the Tigers had a legitimate chance at winning a championship after signing Framber Valdez, Kenley Jansen and bringing back Jack Flaherty and Justin Verlander, among others.

"This wasn’t the way the season was supposed to go. Going into the offseason, [with] the people that we acquired through free agency and who we signed, I’m like, ‘This is the World Series team,’" Skubal said. "This is the team that I’m gonna go and win a World Series and beat anybody. It doesn’t matter what’s going on."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

So even after making his first start with his new team, and incorporating the fact that he was traded away, Skubal wants to return to Detroit. Guess everyone can put down their pitchforks now, right?

Well, no, of course not, because that's not how fans think or operate. But Skubal is correct about what this trade actually means and how the open free agency market works.

The Dodgers could approach Skubal and his agent, Scott Boras, with an extension offer for the remainder of the regular season. They also have a five-day exclusive negotiating window the day after the World Series ends, before free agency starts. But for a player like Skubal, who's expected to get between $300-400 million, reaching the open market carries immense value. More teams bidding increases prices, after all. Especially with big market teams like the Mets or Giants desperate for pitching and capable of making big salary commitments.

So while it's possible he signs with LA, it's unlikely. But the point is that, should Tigers ownership decide they're willing to spend in to bring him back, there's a near certainty they'll have the opportunity. That's how free agency works. And it's why the wailing and gnashing of teeth over this trade was always an exaggerated overreaction.

The Dodgers traded for Yu Darvish in 2017, and let him leave. They traded for Manny Machado in 2018, and saw him sign with San Diego. They traded for Trea Turner and Max Scherzer in 2021, only for Scherzer to leave after that season, while Turner went to Philadelphia in free agency in 2022. They traded for Jack Flaherty in 2024, and he signed with the...Detroit Tigers after winning a World Series in LA.

In fact, outside Tommy Edman, they've never re-signed a player brought in via midseason trade. And Edman is hardly the type of superstar player fans associate with the Dodgers.

Skubal knows that Boras is known for taking advantage of the open market. He knows there's every possibility that he's simply a rental for LA in hopes of a three-peat. And by the way, even after the trade, the Tigers are one of the hottest teams in baseball.

They've won seven of their last 10 games, have passed several teams and are now just two games back of the third wild-card spot in the American League, and three and a half out of first place in the division. They're tied for the best run differential in the AL at +85, and just got top prospect Jackson Jobe back from Tommy John. Imagine if they make a run to the playoffs, bring in Zyhir Hope and River Ryan, and sign Skubal back anyway. Well, none of that would matter because the Dodgers would still have "ruined baseball" regardless.

item.title: Indian national accused of Arizona girlfriend's murder entered US on student visa: federal sources
item.description: Varun Batchigari allegedly strangled Julissa Salazar near the University of Arizona, then boarded a flight to India before the FBI had him arrested.
item.content:encoded:
The man accused of murdering his teenage girlfriend in Arizona allegedly tried to cover his tracks, flee the country and vanish overseas.

Federal law enforcement sources told Fox News the accused killer, 20-year-old Varun Batchigari, is an Indian national who entered the United States through Los Angeles International Airport on Jan. 8, 2024, on an F-1 student visa.

After the alleged killing, authorities say Batchigari boarded a flight from Houston bound for India with a layover in Germany, where he was arrested after the FBI alerted local authorities.

MIGRANT WHO FLED IRELAND AFTER AMERICAN MOTHER'S MURDER IS ARRESTED IN JORDAN

The FBI is now working to extradite him back to Arizona to face a first-degree murder charge.

Batchigari is charged with murdering his 19-year-old girlfriend, Julissa Salazar, who Tucson police say was strangled Thursday inside an off-campus apartment near the University of Arizona.

Investigators allege Batchigari stole Salazar's cellphone and credit cards after the killing, then sent a series of text messages to her mother while posing as the victim in an apparent attempt to conceal the crime. The messages raised concern among Salazar's family, prompting a welfare check that led officers to discover her body.

A felony warrant paints a picture of escalating violence, a deteriorating relationship and mounting personal troubles in the months leading up to Salazar's death.

FITNESS TRAINER TOLD FRIEND SHE WAS 'SCARED FOR HER LIFE' WEEKS BEFORE BODY WITH MATCHING CLOTHING FOUND

According to the warrant, obtained by KOLD-TV, Batchigari had previously been involved in an assault case investigated by the University of Arizona Police Department.

Witnesses interviewed by investigators said Salazar moved out after experiencing problems with Batchigari in late 2025 and had planned to end the relationship because of an alleged history of domestic violence.

The warrant also includes allegations from multiple witnesses describing prior violent behavior. One witness told investigators Batchigari sexually assaulted her at a Halloween party but said she never reported the allegation to law enforcement.

Another witness told investigators Batchigari had been expelled from the University of Arizona following a fight and later lost his job, leading to financial problems and concerns about his student visa status and ability to pay rent.

EXCLUSIVE: DHS SEEKS CUSTODY OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER TRUMP DEPORTATION, BIDEN RELEASE

Federal records reviewed by Fox News show Batchigari remained in lawful immigration status at the time of the alleged murder despite his reported expulsion from the University of Arizona.

Because international students on F-1 visas are generally required to remain enrolled to maintain their legal status, it is unclear why his immigration status had not yet changed.

A Tucson Police Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital there were no updates beyond the information already released publicly. Fox News Digital also reached out to the University of Arizona to confirm Batchigari's enrollment history and whether Salazar was a student, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: 'The Odyssey' inspires surging travel interest in real-world locations behind the blockbuster
item.description: Christopher Nolan filmed "The Odyssey" at stunning real locations across Greece, Sicily, Morocco, Scotland and more. Interest in travel to these areas is surging.
item.content:encoded:
Christopher Nolan's blockbuster film "The Odyssey" takes moviegoers on an epic journey throughout the ancient world — with many of the scenes shot in notable locations all over the world. 

Filming took place at spectacular spots in Greece, Italy, Morocco, Scotland and Iceland — continuing Nolan's longtime preference for practical filmmaking and in-camera effects. 

The film, after just four weekends, has become Nolan's highest grossing movie ever at the global box office, with $1.1 billion pulled in, according to Deadline. ("The Odyssey" is also the highest grossing R-rated movie of 2026 both in North America and around the world, the same source said.)

MEET THE TERRIFYING MONSTERS IN CHRISTOPHER NOLAN'S BLOCKBUSTER 'THE ODYSSEY'

The locations were transformed into a variety of settings, including ancient Troy, Odysseus' homeland of Ithaca and the cave in which the hero encounters the Cyclops. 

Travelers have been showing a strong interest in taking in some of these locations for themselves. A recent analysis from Nibble, a learning app, found that Google search interest in traveling to Troy jumped 3,421% after the movie's mid-July release, while searches for "flights to Troy" increased 966%, as Travel + Leisure reported.  

Searches about whether Troy is a real place or not also surged, the same source noted — "suggesting that many viewers left the theater wondering whether Homer’s legendary city is somewhere they can actually visit," Travel + Leisure said. 

FAMOUS BEACH NOW REQUIRES VISITORS TO RESERVE SPOTS WEEKS AHEAD AND PAY FEES

Moviegovers may recognize the following five locations in the film — and may find a way to see these locations with their own eyes in the days, weeks and months ahead. 

Voidokilia Beach is located in Messenia, in the southwestern Peloponnese region of Greece.

The uniquely shaped beach, which served as one of the film's Greek filming locations, is about 10 miles from the coastal town of Pylos.

Nestor's Cave sits above Voidokilia Beach.

ANCIENT PALACE DISCOVERY CHALLENGES THE MYTH BEHIND SPARTA'S RISE TO POWER

The cave was used to film scenes with Polyphemus, the Cyclops who traps Odysseus and his crew in his cave before devouring several of the men.

Visitors can reach Nestor's Cave on foot via a hiking trail above Voidokilia Beach, though the climb is rocky and steep.

The largest of Sicily's Egadi Islands, Favignana was used to represent Ithaca in "The Odyssey."

Also known as the Aegadian Islands, the archipelago consists of three main islands known for their crystal-clear waters.

Favignana is about a 30-minute ferry ride from Trapani on Sicily's western coast.

EXPERTS STUNNED AFTER UNCOVERING HOMER'S 'ILIAD' ON EGYPTIAN MUMMY IN UNPRECEDENTED FIND

The waters surrounding the Egadi Islands have also yielded remarkable archaeological finds.

In September 2025, Sicilian officials announced the discovery of a well-preserved bronze helmet near the site of the 241 B.C. Battle of the Aegates, along with weapons.

Aït Benhaddou is a fortified settlement in southern Morocco, with structures dating back to the 17th century.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

In "The Odyssey," Aït Benhaddou serves as part of ancient Troy at the end of the Trojan War.

The UNESCO World Heritage Site remains open to visitors and is a roughly 30-minute drive from Ouarzazate.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Marrakech, a popular tourist destination, is roughly 110 miles from Aït Benhaddou.

As for the beach where the Trojan Horse is found and brought ashore — that took place on the beaches of Essaouira, Morocco, on the Atlantic coast, according to multiple reports. 

Nolan filmed scenes at Findlater Castle in Aberdeenshire, on Scotland's northeast coast, last summer, according to several sources.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The castle overlooks the Moray Firth, a large inlet of the North Sea. Visitors can explore the castle, which features ruins dating back to the 14th century, though the first documented fortification at the site dates to 1246.

"For nearly eight centuries, Findlater Castle has stood witness to the ebb and flow of history — from Viking occupation to royal sieges," officials from Findlater Castle said in a statement.

"Now, thanks to Christopher Nolan's vision, these ancient ruins will introduce millions of cinema-goers around the world to the raw beauty of the Banffshire coast."

item.title: Ivanka Trump shares intimate look at cool-weather Iceland getaway with Jared Kushner and their kids
item.description: Stunning photos show Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner bundled up in front of Iceland's waterfalls as the family embraced cooler weather on their recent summer getaway.
item.content:encoded:
Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner swapped the summer heat for Iceland's cooler weather during a recent family getaway filled with waterfalls and outdoor adventures.

Trump shared several stunning photos from the trip on social media, giving her followers a look at the family's time exploring the Nordic country.

The photos showed Trump, 44, and Kushner, 45, taking in Iceland's scenery, including a sweet shot of the couple together in front of a waterfall.

IVANKA TRUMP AND BETTINA ANDERSON’S CLOSE BOND ON DISPLAY AT MAR-A-LAGO BRIDAL SHOWER

Another photo showed Kushner holding his wife as they shared a kiss, with the couple bundled up for the cool Icelandic weather.

Their three children, Arabella, Joseph and Theodore, also joined the trip, with Trump sharing a family photo of the five together outside a rustic home surrounded by greenery.

The family spent time in Iceland's Blue Lagoon, with Trump sharing photos of herself and her two sons taking a dip.

Trump and Kushner have been together for nearly two decades, first meeting in 2007 before marrying in 2009.

POPULAR CITY BANS PUBLIC ALCOHOL AMID HEAT WAVE AS PEOPLE TAKE RISKS TO COOL DOWN

For travelers looking to follow the family's lead, Iceland can make for a "coolcation," a getaway centered around escaping high summer temperatures in favor of a cooler destination.

The country offers milder weather along with plenty of opportunities to explore the outdoors, from waterfalls and hiking trails to hot springs and other natural attractions.

June through August marks the country's busiest travel period, as longer days and milder conditions make it easier for visitors to spend time outside, according to magazine Travel + Leisure.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Even at the height of summer, Iceland remains chilly compared with many traditional vacation spots. Reykjavík generally sees temperatures in the 50s, while the country's northern location means daylight stretches well into the night, Travel + Leisure reported.

Summer also gives travelers access to areas that can be harder to reach at other times of year, including mountain roads and hiking trails. The season is a popular time for whale watching, with June and July among the best months for sightings, according to the publication.

Iceland is not the only destination offering travelers a break from the summer heat.

Norway delivers its own version of a cool-weather escape, pairing temperatures in the high 50s across northern and coastal areas with the long days the region is known for, according to business news outlet Quartz.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Those extra hours of daylight leave more time for travelers to experience the country's fjords, whether from the water, along hiking trails or while exploring Norway's coastal communities, Quartz reported.

Scotland offers another way to trade summer heat for time outdoors, with temperatures topping out around 63 degrees during the season, according to the outlet. Visitors can use the milder weather to explore the Highlands, tour castles or head for the coast.

item.title: Who is DiJonai Carrington? WNBA star who smacked Sophie Cunningham, got ejected and blamed 'White privilege'
item.description: DiJonai Carrington's history of confrontations with Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and WNBA referees reveals a pattern of attention-seeking behavior.
item.content:encoded:
DiJonai Carrington found a way to make it all about her on Saturday.

A routine fast-break layup transformed into the latest flashpoint in the WNBA's national culture war after the Chicago Sky star was ejected after delivering a vicious strike to the head and neck of Indiana Fever sensation Sophie Cunningham. Carrington then went on social media to pour gasoline on the fallout of the foul with her now-infamous "White privilege," remark after her punishment.

Carrington already appears to be looking forward to her next chance to sap of that attention, as she gleefully posted the date of the Sky's rematch against the Fever on Aug. 23.

WNBA FACES DISCIPLINE DILEMMA AFTER CARRINGTON'S 'WHITE PRIVILEGE' POST TARGETING INDIANA FEVER

And while this latest stunt has become a national headline, it's hardly the first time Carrington has leveraged the Fever to make herself the center of attention.

How did she get here?

Religion played a major role in her home life.

Her father became a pastor, her mother is active in ministry, and DiJonai attended a private Christian school growing up.

Her father, Darren Carrington, was a standout safety in the NFL who played in two Super Bowls during his eight-year professional career.

Her mother, Vickie, was a star track athlete.

Inspired by her older siblings (brother Darren II and sister Diarra), she insisted on playing youth football in elementary school, playing one year of flag football and two years of tackle football in grades 2 through 4.

During her high school years at Horizon Christian Academy in San Diego, her mother served as her basketball head coach, her father as the associate head coach and her sister as an assistant coach.

DiJonai became a highly touted prospect who played for elite programs, beginning her college career at Stanford University.

In a 2019 interview for "My Stanford Story," Carrington spoke modestly and eloquently about her childhood and overcoming injuries, and her academic interests in psychology and African American studies.

She later transferred to Baylor before being drafted by the Connecticut Sun in 2021.

Fast forward to 2026, Carrington has a very different image than what she put on display in her 2019 Stanford interview.

Just weeks before her confrontation with Cunningham, Carrington sent shockwaves through the WNBA by publicly detonating her former relationship on social media.

During the late-July All-Star break, Carrington took to Threads to launch a spontaneous, unprovoked attack on her ex-girlfriend, Las Vegas Aces forward NaLyssa Smith.

The two had dated since their college days at Baylor in 2020 and even briefly played together for the Dallas Wings.

A full year after their breakup, Carrington suddenly accused Smith of cheating on her with multiple other WNBA players, explicitly naming Deja Kelly and Aaliyah Nye in the process to her followers.

DIJONAI CARRINGTON DECLARES 'WHITE PRIVILEGE' AFTER EJECTION FOR SMACKING SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM IN THE FACE

"Since mfs wanna be funny today ima be hilarious!" Carrington wrote on social media, dragging uninvolved players into a chaotic, reality-TV-style scandal on a random Sunday morning.

Smith, clearly blindsided by the sudden accusations, was forced to defend herself on a Twitch livestream.

Calling the outburst "weird" and questioning why Carrington would bring a year-old private issue to the internet, Smith pleaded for the privacy of the other players dragged into the mess.

"These folks is minding they business," Smith said on Twitch. "These folks woke up to this [expletive] on a random Sunday night of these types of allegations."

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT AGAINST DIJONAI CARRINGTON AFTER FLAGRANT FOUL AND 'WHITE PRIVILEGE' POST

Their relationship had been one of the most widely-known and discussed pairings in the WNBA in recent years. But Carrington had previously claimed that she wasn't even gay, while they were still together.

"I'm not even like into girls... I'm not gay, I just like Lyss," Carrington said, adding that Smith would never have to worry about Carrington being into other girls, or other guys, during an appearance on Angel Reese's podcast in March 2025.

Carrington has also used her basketball platform to make her progressive political allegiances unmistakable.

Days after President Donald Trump began his second term in January 2025, Carrington arrived at an Unrivaled game wearing a vintage sweatshirt from rapper YG’s "F— Donald Trump Tour." The garment featured the rapper raising his middle fingers beneath the tour’s name.

Carrington then amplified the display by posting photographs of the outfit to X with the caption, "what my hoodie says."

Less than a week later, Carrington called on the WNBA to respond to the new administration during an Unrivaled press conference.

"We see that some of the policies are already going into action," Carrington said, adding that it was "time for us to also take action."

Carrington cited threats to women’s and LGBTQ rights, although she did not identify what specific action she expected the WNBA or its players to take.

WHITE HOUSE DEFENDS WNBA STAR SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM AFTER SHE SPEAKS OUT IN SUPPORT OF PROTECTING WOMEN'S SPORTS

Her political commentary later intersected directly with the Fever rivalry.

In the days before her confrontation with Cunningham, Carrington inserted herself into the national dispute over transgender participation in women’s sports. Cunningham had argued that girls and women should not be required to compete against athletes she described as biological men, a position that drew criticism from former U.S. soccer star Megan Rapinoe.

When Rapinoe attacked Cunningham’s position and her association with conservative activist Riley Gaines, Carrington signaled her approval beneath Rapinoe’s Instagram video.

"Clock it, Megan!" Carrington wrote.

During the opening round of the 2024 WNBA Playoffs, Carrington delivered a brutal blow directly to the eye of then-rookie sensation Caitlin Clark.

The uncalled foul left the league's biggest star with a prominent black eye and sparked outrage from fans and commentators who suspected the hit was entirely intentional. Rather than apologizing or showing concern, Carrington dismissed the backlash, telling reporters it "doesn't even make sense" that she would purposefully injure a player.

Carrington didn't just brush off the eye-poke controversy; she actively mocked it.

Weeks after the incident, Carrington went on Instagram Live and performed a coordinated bit where she was supposedly accidentally poked in the eye while cooking. Smiling and laughing at the camera, she repeatedly asked, "Did you do it on purpose?"—a blatant, theatrical mockery of USA Today reporter Christine Brennan, who had dared to ask Carrington during a press conference if the hit on Clark was intentional.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Carrington also shared that she had received a severely abusive and threatening email from an anonymous sender. She posted a screenshot of the message to her Instagram Stories, revealing that it contained a racial slur alongside graphic death and sexual assault threats, specifically stating, "I hope someone rapes you and cuts your head off."

The WNBA later issued a formal statement denouncing the toxic behavior. The league condemned any racist, derogatory, or threatening comments directed at its players and announced that its security team was actively monitoring threat-related activity, with plans to involve law enforcement when necessary.

On Aug. 28, 2024, after a game where Carrington's Sun lost to Clark's Fever, Carrington posted a brief comment on social media regarding the Fever fan base.

"The indiana fever have the nastiest fans in the W. ew," she wrote on X.

During that August 2024 game, there were moments of on-court back-and-forth, including a sequence where Carrington shushed the crowd shortly before Clark scored a basket. Carrington provided no specific details in her initial post about what prompted her assertion regarding the fans' behavior.

Carrington’s "White privilege" accusation was not the first time she transformed a disagreement with WNBA officials into an allegation of social bias.

On May 29, 2025, Carrington’s Dallas Wings suffered a 97-92 loss to the Sky at Wintrust Arena. Carrington scored 15 points, but her most memorable performance came after the final buzzer.

Carrington approached head official Roy Gulbeyan near midcourt and began arguing about the officiating. Video shows an animated but nonphysical exchange as Carrington continued moving toward Gulbeyan.

After listening for several seconds, Gulbeyan motioned for arena security.

A security guard stepped between them while Gulbeyan retreated behind him, at one point gripping the guard’s shirt as Carrington continued speaking.

The following day, Carrington posted footage of the encounter to X and suggested that Gulbeyan’s response was a microaggression.

"security… when i’m literally having a civil conversation is insane," Carrington wrote. "mind you, he called the ‘sEcUrItY’ over there… #Mircoagression."

WNBA legend Sheryl Swoopes rushed to Carrington’s defense, declaring that if the referee felt afraid and needed security, he "should NEVER be able to ref again."

Days later, a foul she committed against Ariel Atkins was upgraded to a flagrant 1. On June 3, she received another flagrant 1 after striking Seattle’s Skylar Diggins-Smith in the head while attempting to block a layup.

Carrington again turned to social media, rejecting the growing description of her as a dirty player. She insisted that she simply "play[s] hard" and is "ALWAYS" attempting to make a play on the ball, while claiming that other recent flagrant rulings had been rescinded after challenges.

Despite her hair being black in her 2019 Stanford interview, Carrington previously claimed her hair is naturally blonde.

"I hate when people talk about that, like, 'Why do you have blonde hair?' I got black eyebrows. I got black arm hair, black leg hair ... and I don't care. I'm still a natural blonde," she said during her March 2025 appearance on Reese’s podcast.

item.title: Fetterman 'dares' El-Sayed to stick with Piker, claims Michigan nominee has 'little man syndrome energy'
item.description: John Fetterman says Abdul El-Sayed's anti-Israel views and alliance with Hasan Piker have put Michigan's critical Senate seat in play for Democrats.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., warned Friday that Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed could cost his party a must-hold Michigan Senate seat, escalating a personal feud over El-Sayed’s campaign style, opposition to military aid for Israel and alliance with far-left streamer Hasan Piker.

"He has put, you know, that seat in play," Fetterman said during an interview with The Washington Post. "And after Bernie Sanders and others created the disaster in Maine, and they pushed garbage person like Platner, and now they’ve pushed an individual like El-Sayed that’s been very proud of his very deeply anti-Israel views and proud to campaign with an avowed communist overall."

The Michigan contest is one of roughly a dozen races expected to determine control of the Senate.

El-Sayed defeated establishment-backed Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich. More than $80 million poured into the primary, the most expensive Democratic Senate nomination contest in history.

El-Sayed will face former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers for retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters' seat.

EL-SAYED PALS AROUND WITH FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER THE DAY BEFORE CRUCIAL MICHIGAN SENATE ELECTION

Piker had made repeated appearances with El-Sayed, including at a Detroit pool party the night before the primary. The streamer has previously said America "deserved 9/11" and praised Mao Zedong as "one of the great leaders of this world."

El-Sayed has said he does not share all of Piker’s positions but resisted calls to distance himself.

The Republican National Committee seized on El-Sayed’s ties to Piker, accusing Democrats of failing to confront the nominee’s political associations.

"El-Sayed is a terrorist sympathizer and an America-hating socialist. His refusal to distance himself from Hamas-hugging radicals like Hasan Piker reaffirms his true allegiance is to terrorist groups, not America," RNC National Spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre told Fox News Digital on Sunday.

She continued, "Democrats' refusal to disavow this clown shows they either share his poisonous ideology or they're too cowardly to confront it."

SEE IT: MICHIGAN DEM PREDICTS FAR-LEFT EL-SAYED WILL WIN SENATE RACE AFTER BACKING HIS PRIMARY RIVAL

Fetterman challenged El-Sayed to maintain that relationship as he moved beyond the Democratic primary electorate.

"I dare you to continue to campaign with people like Hasan Piker because he now will quickly find out it’s easy to campaign in the echo chamber as a Democrat," Fetterman said.

Fetterman's warning broke with Peters, who backed Stevens but who told Fox News Digital that El-Sayed would defeat Rogers because of the candidates' differences on issues affecting Michigan families.

"And in the end, that’s why he will prevail," Peters said.

The dispute turned personal after Washington Post host Kate Andrews played a clip of El-Sayed criticizing Fetterman’s approach to Midwestern politics and temperament.

DEMS' LEFTWARD LURCH GETS LEGS AS EL-SAYED'S MICHIGAN SENATE VICTORY SPARKS PARTY DEBATE

"Fetterman is probably the biggest issue. Fetterman is the sitting counterargument to the kind of Midwest politics that I think really can work," El-Sayed said. "He’s also just an a——. I try to give him the benefit of the doubt. It’s just he seems miserable, and he seems like he doesn’t like the job."

Fetterman answered by pointing to El-Sayed's conduct during the primary.

"He just has like this weird little man syndrome energy just going around insulting people," Fetterman said. "And, you know, that’s the kind of campaign that he’s run."

El-Sayed had sought to reassure Democrats before the primary that he would unite supporters of his rivals against Rogers.

"I think everybody understands what the stakes are. So I’m looking forward to welcoming everybody who might have voted differently in the primary," El-Sayed previously told Fox News Digital.

That unity effort suffered an early setback Friday when former House Judiciary Committee Democratic chief counsel Julian Epstein told Fox News Digital that he would support Rogers, saying the Democratic Party had moved too far left and "lost its moral center."

item.title: WNBA’s lack of clarity on gender eligibility policy is ‘herald of the times culturally,’ ex-NBA player says
item.description: Royce White says the WNBA's failure to define "woman" in its CBA is a cultural herald, as Cathy Engelbert addresses transgender athlete concerns.
item.content:encoded:
Royce White, a former NBA player who said he will declare for the 2027 WNBA Draft, said Sunday the league is an "example" of "us losing a lot of things in this country."

White appeared on Fox News Channel’s "Fox & Friends Weekend" and was asked whether the league was at risk of losing its new audience amid the growing trans athlete debate surrounding the league and the lack of a clear policy when it came to gender eligibility.

FORMER NBA PLAYER ROYCE WHITE SAYS HE IS DECLARING FOR NEXT WNBA DRAFT AFTER ENES KANTER ANNOUNCEMENT

"The WNBA is an example of a herald of us losing a lot of things in this country," White said. "We have to secure our elections, we have to restart the mass deportations, we have to start arresting some of these Deep Staters, I’m a huge fan of banning Sharia Law and Marxism nationwide and also some of these PACs and lobbies, but the WNBA and their lack of terminology, precision is a herald of the times culturally, for sure."

The WNBA’s collective bargaining agreement’s Article XIII, Section 1(a) states: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." But as OutKick/Fox News Digital previously reported, the 409-page agreement never defines "woman" or "women." The terms "transgender" and "gender identity" don’t appear anywhere in the document.

The CBA contains detailed definitions for dozens of other terms. Yet the agreement doesn’t define the word that determines who may play in the league.

"It’s just astounding that the WNBA can’t define the ‘W’ in the name," White added. "I think we’re going through a very necessary conversation about who’s actually eligible to play in some of these sports leagues I guess on both sides of the gender spectrum. My goal is to help elevate the WNBA. I think the ticket prices and the attendance will soar. I think the live audience will increase and I think, ultimately, it’s good for the game.

"It’s gonna help evolve the game. I mean, who would argue that a player like myself or an Enes Kanter (Freedom) or in the future, maybe a LeBron James after he expires in the NBA, maybe he wakes up and he realizes he’s a woman as well, who could argue that wouldn’t make the women’s game better?"

WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert sent a letter to teams on Friday addressing concerns over the inclusion of transgender athletes in the league as White and Kanter Freedom said they wanted to declare for the draft.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I know many of you have received questions in recent weeks regarding transgender athlete participation in women’s basketball, and I expect this topic will continue to receive significant attention," Engelbert wrote in the memo, per The Associated Press.

"I wanted to reach out to share how we are approaching these conversations at the league office and to thank those of you who have responded to questions from the media with thoughtfulness and professionalism."

Engelbert went on to call the debate "nuanced."

"We recognize that this is a complex and nuanced topic, and we will continue to have important conversations with all of you and the Players Association in the weeks and months ahead," Engelbert said in the memo. "We also plan to convene additional discussions and offer listening sessions for any team leaders who would like to participate. Your perspectives and feedback are invaluable, and I appreciate those who have already reached out to share their thoughts."

As far as the WNBA Draft, White said on "Fox & Friends Weekend" he was "having a blast in my feminine era."

"I never thought that I was a woman I always trusted the science," he said. "I thought that I was a man my entire life. After further review, strong look at my personal preferences, it would appear, indeed, that sometimes I identify as a transgender woman. And I think it’s only fair that I get a chance to play with some of my queens here in the twilight of my career, my athletic prime."

Fox News’ Dan Zaksheske contributed to this report.

item.title: Police nab 'armed and dangerous' New York fugitive suspected of killing father and torching home
item.description: Thomas David Ryan was captured in Schoharie County after a multiday New York manhunt involving the FBI in his father's homicide and arson case.
item.content:encoded:
An "armed and dangerous" New York fugitive suspected of killing his 70-year-old father and setting the family home ablaze was captured Sunday, ending a multiday manhunt that drew in the FBI and police agencies across the state.

Thomas David Ryan, 32, was taken into custody in the Gilboa area of Schoharie County, New York State Police said. Authorities had been searching for Ryan since his father, Robert Ryan, was found dead inside his burning Greenville home Thursday evening. Police said the fire was deliberately set.

Police did not say how Ryan was found or provide details about his arrest. They said more information would be released later.

NEW YORK STATE POLICE LAUNCH MANHUNT AFTER KILLING, HOUSE FIRE FOR 'ARMED AND DANGEROUS' SUSPECT

The case began around 7:30 p.m. Thursday, when state troopers were called to a house fire on Greenville Turnpike in Orange County.

After firefighters put out the blaze, a man was found dead inside the home. Police later identified him as Robert Ryan, 70.

Investigators determined the fire had been set intentionally and began treating Robert Ryan’s death as a homicide. Police soon began searching for his son.

Ryan did not live with his father and had no other known ties to the Greenville area at the time, according to State Police.

'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN

Investigators believed Ryan left in his father’s gray 2016 Toyota Prius. As the search widened, police repeatedly described him as "armed and dangerous" and urged anyone who spotted him to call 911 rather than approach him.

Police combed through surveillance video from homes and businesses, trying to trace Ryan’s movements after the killing. Residents in Greenville and nearby communities were asked to check footage recorded from about 6 p.m. Thursday through the overnight hours.

Police said Ryan had stayed at shelters across New York and was known to frequent the Plattsburgh area, more than 200 miles north of Greenville. Investigators checked places where he had previously stayed and worked with rail operators because Ryan was known to travel by train.

The investigation eventually involved the FBI, NYPD, the Orange County Sheriff’s Office and police departments in Middletown and Port Jervis, along with several State Police investigative units and other state and county agencies.

Police have not disclosed a possible motive, how Robert Ryan died or what charges Thomas Ryan faces.

item.title: NORAD fighter jets intercept 2 aircraft near Trump’s golf club, 3rd plane delays his NJ departure
item.description: NORAD intercepted two general aviation aircraft over Bedminster after they entered restricted airspace near President Donald Trump’s New Jersey golf club.
item.content:encoded:
Officials said at least three general aviation aircraft violated temporary flight restrictions near Bedminster, New Jersey, on Sunday as President Donald Trump spent the weekend at his golf club, where the four-day LIV Golf New York tournament was being held.

The North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD) said its F-16 fighter jets intercepted two general aviation aircraft before confirming that a third aircraft also triggered an alert as Trump was preparing to depart the area.

The third incident appeared to delay Trump’s departure by about 13 minutes. During that time, emergency SUVs, law enforcement officers and U.S. Secret Service agents were seen moving into position near the runway where Trump was scheduled to depart around 5 p.m. E.T.

Officials said the first two general aviation aircraft were safely escorted out of the restricted area by NORAD aircraft. The third aircraft "reestablished communications and became compliant before NORAD intervention was required."

PRESIDENT TRUMP RECEIVES BIG CHEERS FROM SPECTATORS DURING LIV GOLF EVENT AT HIS NEW JERSEY CLUB

Video captured one of the first two interceptions, showing the dramatic moment an F-16 fighter jet closed in on what appeared to be a small Cessna aircraft near Jefferson Township, outside Bedminster.

Ahead of Trump landing in New Jersey, NORAD previously said that it would enforce multiple FAA-established temporary flight restrictions over the region this weekend. 

Pilots and the public were also told that U.S. Army ground-based defense assets may be present in the area, operating under the Continental U.S. NORAD Region as part of the command’s routine, layered defense. 

"These systems are operating under NORAD authorities, constitute a routine component of the command’s layered defense posture and work in tandem with the command’s airborne assets to monitor and protect the airspace," information published by the Defense Visual Information Distribution Service said. 

TRUMP DRAWS MUCH DIFFERENT REACTION AT NBA FINALS THAN HE DID AT CFP NATIONAL TITLE GAME

Officials used the incident to remind general aviation pilots to check Notices to Airmen (NOTAMs) before every flight for the latest information on airspace restrictions and other flight procedures, as required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). 

"Check NOTAMs before EVERY flight!" 1st AF/AFNORTH said in a post on X. 

If a pilot becomes intercepted by NORAD aircraft, the pilot should immediately adjust their radio frequency to 121.5 or 243.0, according to information published by the Defense Visual Information Distribution Service. 

They should then "turn around to reverse course until receiving additional instructions on one of those frequencies."

Temporary flight restrictions are often issued to limit aircraft operations in designated areas for presidential movements, major sporting events, national security concerns and other special events. 

NORAD often employs a network of radars, satellites, fighter aircraft and other capabilities to identify and respond to potential threats in the North American airspace.
